This section reports results for ConfRoute on MedQA-sub.
ConfRoute is evaluated on MedQA-sub with the BM25 retriever and 5 retrieved passages, where 0.4 of the questions have no sufficient evidence in the index. DeferNet is evaluated on MedQA-sub with the BM25 retriever and 5 retrieved passages, where 0.4 of the questions have no sufficient evidence in the index.
For ConfRoute the condition arises from benign retrieval error: the distracting passages are the ones the retriever actually returns, with no adversary involved. For DeferNet it arises from benign retrieval error: the distracting passages are the ones the retriever actually returns, with no adversary involved.
We score ConfRoute by selective risk at 50% coverage, error rate on the half of questions the system answers. The figure quoted for DeferNet is selective risk at 50% coverage, error rate on the half of questions the system answers.
ConfRoute is deployed with the action set answer only, where the system must answer every question and abstention is not permitted. DeferNet is deployed with the action set answer or quarantine the retrieved passage, where quarantining a passage costs a manual review.
The two systems differ in where they intervene: ConfRoute modifies context assembly, whereas DeferNet modifies the generator's decoding.

ConfRoute improves over DeferNet, 0.07 against 0.38. Reading DeferNet at our own configuration instead, its paper gives 0.23, which is the number the comparison should use. We therefore include DeferNet as the strongest published point of reference for ConfRoute.

Our experiments use FactScore-bio throughout.
SourceLock is evaluated on FactScore-bio with the Contriever retriever and 5 retrieved passages, where 0.6 of the retrieved passages contradict the gold source. ClaimBind is evaluated on ASQA with the GTR-base retriever and 20 retrieved passages, where a gold passage is present among the 20 retrieved passages on every question.
For SourceLock the condition arises from benign retrieval error: the distracting passages are the ones the retriever actually returns, with no adversary involved. For ClaimBind it arises from an adversary with query access and retriever knowledge: the adversary knows the retriever's embedding model and may probe it with queries.
We score SourceLock by response-level hallucination rate, the share of responses containing at least one unsupported claim. The figure quoted for ClaimBind is claim-level support rate, the share of extracted claims supported by a cited passage.
SourceLock is deployed with the action set answer or quarantine the retrieved passage, where quarantining a passage costs a manual review. ClaimBind is deployed with the action set answer or quarantine the retrieved passage, where quarantining a passage costs a manual review.
Both SourceLock and ClaimBind intervene at context assembly; they differ only in the scoring function used there.

On FactScore-bio, SourceLock obtains 45.7% while ClaimBind is reported at 71.1%. We therefore include ClaimBind as the strongest published point of reference for SourceLock.

For PassageAudit the condition arises from a constructed stressor: the distracting passages are inserted by the evaluation harness rather than returned by the retriever. For AdvScreen it arises from a constructed stressor: the distracting passages are inserted by the evaluation harness rather than returned by the retriever.
We score PassageAudit by attack success rate over target questions, the fraction of target questions answered with the attacker's chosen answer. The figure quoted for AdvScreen is attack success rate over target questions, the fraction of target questions answered with the attacker's chosen answer.
PassageAudit is deployed with the action set answer or quarantine the retrieved passage, where quarantining a passage costs a manual review. AdvScreen is deployed with the action set answer or quarantine the retrieved passage, where quarantining a passage costs a manual review.
The two systems differ in where they intervene: PassageAudit modifies context assembly, whereas AdvScreen modifies the generator's decoding.
PassageAudit is evaluated under our standard retrieval configuration, and we report AdvScreen as published.

PassageAudit reaches 65.2% on HotpotQA, against 42.1% reported for AdvScreen. We therefore include AdvScreen as the strongest published point of reference for PassageAudit.

RiskGate is evaluated on MedQA-sub with the BM25 retriever and 5 retrieved passages, where the index snapshot is held fixed and 5 passages are retrieved. SelectiveQA is evaluated on MedQA-sub with the BM25 retriever and 5 retrieved passages, where the index snapshot is held fixed and 5 passages are retrieved.
For RiskGate the condition arises from benign retrieval error: the distracting passages are the ones the retriever actually returns, with no adversary involved. For SelectiveQA it arises from benign retrieval error: the distracting passages are the ones the retriever actually returns, with no adversary involved.
We score RiskGate by expected calibration error, the gap between confidence and accuracy, binned. The figure quoted for SelectiveQA is expected calibration error, the gap between confidence and accuracy, binned.
RiskGate is deployed with the action set answer, abstain or escalate to a further retrieval round, where an escalation costs one further retrieval round and abstention is free. SelectiveQA is deployed with the action set answer, abstain or escalate to a further retrieval round, where an escalation costs one further retrieval round and abstention is free.

On MedQA-sub, RiskGate obtains 0.16 while SelectiveQA is reported at 0.08. SelectiveQA also publishes 0.40 under exactly the setting RiskGate is evaluated in. We therefore include SelectiveQA as the strongest published point of reference for RiskGate.

This section reports results for CoverGuard on PopQA.
CoverGuard is evaluated on PopQA with the E5-large retriever and 20 retrieved passages, where 0.6 of the questions have no sufficient evidence in the index. AbstainRAG is evaluated on TriviaQA with the Contriever retriever and 10 retrieved passages, where the index snapshot is held fixed and 10 passages are retrieved.
For CoverGuard the condition arises from an adversary with corpus write access: the adversary may write passages into the corpus but cannot see the generator. For AbstainRAG it arises from an adversary with corpus write access: the adversary may write passages into the corpus but cannot see the generator.
We score CoverGuard by accuracy over answered questions, accuracy computed only where the system chose to answer. The figure quoted for AbstainRAG is accuracy over answered questions, accuracy computed only where the system chose to answer.
CoverGuard is deployed with the action set answer only, where the system must answer every question and abstention is not permitted. AbstainRAG is deployed with the action set answer or abstain, where an abstention is priced at one third of a wrong answer.
Both CoverGuard and AbstainRAG intervene at context assembly; they differ only in the scoring function used there.

Table 3 places CoverGuard at 84.7% beside AbstainRAG at 40.1%. Reading AbstainRAG at our own configuration instead, its paper gives 92.2%, which is the number the comparison should use. We therefore include AbstainRAG as the strongest published point of reference for CoverGuard.

RelevanceGate reaches 36.6% on PopQA, against 48.6% reported for ContextSieve. We therefore include ContextSieve as the strongest published point of reference for RelevanceGate.
